undock.release_note: The magnet pairs are slid sideways by a cam ring before the pumps pull back: 6 x 18.2 N of shear instead of 547 N of pull.

checks.text: Gel surface inside the shell 31 mm under the outer waterline: the dome air sits at 308 Pa and holds the gel down (diving bell).
The opening is under water: its top is 51 mm below the waterline and 20 mm below the inner gel surface.
Gel at the open opening: density excess gives 6.5 Pa of drive against a 25 Pa yield stress, so the gel stays in the shell.
Kit held by the gel after release: needs 14.5 Pa (kit density 1476 kg/m3), gel has 25 Pa.
Every G-code point is inside the DexArm reach (200 mm stem, base on a 140 mm shelf rail): worst position error 0.00 mm, 0 points at a joint limit.
After the kit is placed the vertical stem never passes through the kit (2 mm margin): 0 hits.
DexArm push stays under its 0.5 kg payload (4.9 N): peak 2.51 N.
ECO62 push stays under its 2 kg payload (19.6 N): peak 2.52 N.
Click: the magnets pull the tail in the last 20 mm; it meets the 3 mm silicone bumpers at 340 mm/s, contact peak 591 N; six pairs then hold 105 N against 10 N of dome air on the face.
The newborn floats: 69 % of its 0.96 L is under water, 28 mm above the surface.
Push tube bending (6 x 4 mm stainless, 100 mm lever): 15 MPa with the DexArm, 15 MPa with the ECO62, against about 200 MPa yield.
